research_question: Does the frozen E045 three-line selector evaluate the consecutive-pair penalty and lexicographic tie-break on the sorted six-number ticket, as required by its preregistration?
novelty_statement: A static comparison found that E045 enumerates six-number combinations in score-ranked candidate-pool order, but computes consecutive adjacency and lexicographic tie-break on that unsorted order. E075 preserves E045 as the legacy comparator and changes only those two order-dependent operations. Both portfolios are built independently with separate used-number sets. The same cutoff-safe predictions and role scores are used; the top-16 candidate-pool ranking rule, model weights, line order, exact null, random seed, alpha, block size, and strict gates remain unchanged. Later available candidate-pool contents may differ only because earlier selected lines differ. This is an implementation-conformance correction, not a new signal family or independent sample.

source_models.source_note: This is a new three-line disjoint portfolio allocator over the existing frozen 11-model B/AC signal set. It is not an independent signal-family claim and does not reuse E019 outcomes as evidence.

line_selection.global_support: Existing frozen rolling reliability-weighted support across all 11 models.
line_selection.candidate_pool: Among numbers not used by earlier lines, sort by descending role score, descending global support, then ascending number; retain the first 16.
line_selection.ticket_objective: Enumerate all six-number combinations in the candidate pool and maximize sum(role_score) - 0.022*abs(odd_count-3) - 0.020*abs(count_at_most_22-3) - 0.010*max(0,consecutive_pairs-2) + 0.004*occupied_decade_bands.
line_selection.cross_line_rule: Numbers selected in an earlier line are unavailable to every later line. Exactly three pairwise-disjoint six-number lines and exactly 18 unique numbers are required.
line_selection.ticket_order_semantics: For each candidate six-number subset, sort the six numbers ascending before counting consecutive adjacent pairs and before applying the lexicographically lower sorted-ticket tie-break. Candidate-pool ranking remains role_score descending, global_score descending, then number ascending; retain the first 16 unused numbers for each role.

random_comparator.method: For each target, apply a uniformly sampled permutation of labels 1..45 jointly to the three fixed model tickets. This preserves exactly three six-number lines, pairwise disjointness, union size 18, and the target-specific incidence geometry.

inference.ci_method: Two-sided percentile moving-block bootstrap of per-target differences from the exact geometry-matched null; sample overlapping contiguous blocks, preserving the fixed final remainder-block length.
inference.block_share_method: Non-overlapping consecutive 50-target blocks; include the final remainder block.

prospective_confirmation.readiness_rule: Historical gate results are diagnostic only. Do not write STRICT_PASS_READY or release purchase lines until the policy owner has explicitly specified the minimum prospective target count and completion rule.

implementation_correction.legacy_behavior: The frozen runner enumerates combinations in score-ranked pool order and evaluates consecutive adjacency plus tuple tie-break in that order, although the preregistered objective specifies a sorted ticket.
implementation_correction.corrected_behavior: Sort each candidate six-number subset before consecutive-pair calculation and lexicographic tie-break; return the sorted ticket.

repair_of_attempt_1.repair_reason: Attempt 1 incorrectly used one shared used-number set for both legacy and corrected portfolios. V2 now maintains independent disjointness state for each portfolio.

promotion_rule: The corrected implementation is not a model promotion. Apply the existing historical strict gate unchanged to the corrected implementation. Even a historical gate pass cannot create STRICT_PASS_READY because prospective confirmation remains required and unspecified. Never generate purchase lines from this study.
